hypotheses.justification: Nothing in the statement or the proof needs N ≠ 0. In Definitions/Def_ModularCurve_X1.lean, x1FunctionFieldC, x1FunctionField, x1FunctionFieldBar and JOne are defined for any M : ℕ with no NeZero assumption. The Galois action σ • _ on JOne N comes from arithmeticGalois and the SMul/DistribMulAction instances in Def_ModularCurve_ArithmeticGalois.lean, which never mention NeZero. The GalIsoX1ClassImpl lemmas the proof calls (pair_nsmul_left, pair_sub_left), as well as pair_zero_left and pair_ne_zero, are stated for any fields K, F and assume only [NeZero n] and [HasPrincipalDivisors K F], nothing about N. The remaining lemmas used (pair_semilinearSmul, SemilinearAut.coe_torsion_smul, ValuationSubring.smul_eq_self_of_mem_inertiaSubgroupIn_of_pow_eq_one) were not opened, but they are applied to objects (g, W, σ, Pl, ζ) whose construction does not involve the NeZero N instance. The case N = 0 is not special: Gamma1 0 and its function field are still defined, and the argument (pair z y is an n-th root of unity, p ∤ n so inertia fixes it, then bilinearity) goes through unchanged. So the same proof compiles without [NeZero N].
